Yahweh is making a conditional statement that sounds hypothetical, but he knows that the condition is not true. **Moses** and **Samuel** had died long before this time, so they could not stand before him and plead for the people. He is stating it as a condition to show that any willingness on his part to spare **this people** is also not true. Use a natural form in your language for introducing a condition that the speaker believes is not true. Alternate translation: [Even if Moses and Samuel were to stand before me, I still would not feel favorable toward this people]

The implication is that **Moses** and **Samuel** were remembered as men whose prayers had turned Yahweh’s anger away from the people in the past. הָי֨וֹ תִֽהְיֶ֥ה לִ⁠י֙ כְּמ֣וֹ אַכְזָ֔ב מַ֖יִם לֹ֥א נֶאֱמָֽנוּ

Jeremiah is using the question form to accuse Yahweh of failing him when he needs help. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [You have become to me like a deceptive brook, like unreliable waters!]

The point of this comparison is that just as a **deceptive {brook}** is unreliable and may fail a traveler who needs water, so Yahweh seems to Jeremiah to be unreliable and to fail him when he needs help. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [unreliable, like a brook that fails a thirsty traveler when he needs it, like waters that a person cannot depend upon]

In this verse Yahweh repeats a single word from the original language in several different senses, “return,” “restore,” and “turn.” This is poetic language. If your language has a way to indicate poetry, you could use it here.

Here Yahweh is speaking as if Jeremiah’s repenting were a physical **return** to him. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [If you turn back from your sin]

Yahweh is using **stand to my face** as a common expression of the culture to mean “serve me as my prophet.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [you shall serve me as my prophet]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if Jeremiah’s speech were metallic ore from which he could **take out the precious** and leave behind what is **worthless**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And if you speak what is valuable instead of what is worthless]

Yahweh is using the adjective **precious** as a noun to mean “something of great value.” Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [what is precious] or [what is of great value]

The point of this comparison is that just as a person’s **mouth** speaks that person’s own words, so Jeremiah will speak Yahweh’s own words to the people. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [you will speak my own words to them]
יָשֻׁ֤בוּ הֵ֨מָּה֙ אֵלֶ֔י⁠ךָ וְ⁠אַתָּ֖ה לֹֽא־תָשׁ֥וּב אֲלֵי⁠הֶֽם

Here Yahweh is speaking as if accepting what someone says were a matter of physically turning toward that person, so **They themselves shall turn to you** means that the people would accept what Jeremiah tells them. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [They themselves shall accept what you say, but you yourself shall not accept what they say]

These two clauses mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [And I will surely rescue you from the power of wicked and ruthless people]
